newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon bank shares end week up, Solidere mixed. [CORRECTED 13:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Lebanon bank shares end week up, Solidere mixed. [CORRECTED 13:05 GMT]

text.p: Bank shares rose while Solidere were mixed on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the week ended on Friday and dealers said Banque Audi was expected to continue a rally next week.
Banque Audi, which has performed strongly since its January 20 debut, closed at $19 from last week's $18.25. Weekly turnover in the bank shares was 82,549 from 87,914 last week.
"There is still high demand for Audi shares which I expect to trade between $20 and $21 in two weeks' time," a dealer, who wished not to be identified, told Reuters.
The other listed bank, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce, rose to $13.625 from $13.125 on increased turnover of 61,831 shares from 42,025 last week.

Solidere A shares, which hit on Monday a new record low of $10.125 on Monday, ended the week at last Friday's $10.25. The shares are distributed to former holders of property rights in central Beirut.
"Most of the supply orders of A shares that have created the oversupply problem in recent weeks have been executed. Thus the problem will be almost over next week," the dealer said.
Solidere B shares, issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994, rose to $10.75 from $10.625.
"I expect considerable demand for B shares to allow the shares to continue trading around $10.75 next week," the dealer said.
A total of 1,084,283 Solidere shares were traded compared with 747,681 a week earlier.
The BLOM stock index fell 0.27 percent on the week to 894.09 while the LISPI share index rose 1.17 percent on the week to 83.33. (Corrects from "rose 0.6 percent to 82.37.")
Also traded were 5,500 Ciment Libanais at $$1.1875 compared with 10,000 shares traded at $1.15625 last week.
There was no trade in the three other listed firms throughout the week: Uniceramic, Eternit shares and Ciments Blancs.
The market's total weekly turnover rose to 1,319,707 from 921,420 and value was $13,730,125 against $9,955,180.
